title: Weighted commitment prober and gateway backpressure gating
author: Asha Raman
release_notes: Introduces a weighted commitment prober and gateway backpressure gate to improve SLA conformance for Dedicated fleets. Adds new metrics and a gradual canary rollout; configurable via FleetPolicy.
description:
Motivation: We observed a class of incidents where reserved-capacity tenants consume their committed slots in bursts while heavily overcommitting queued but not-yet-started requests, causing transient SLO violations for other tenants and unstable autoscaler behavior. This PR implements two complementary pieces: (1) a lightweight 'commitment prober' that continuously simulates weighted commitment realizations across tenants to estimate near-term conformance risk, and (2) a gateway-level backpressure gate that enforces soft throttles for low-priority or speculative requests when projected conformance falls below configured thresholds.

Design summary: The commitment prober runs in the control-plane as a sampling job. It consumes per-tenant reservation ledgers and recent utilization histograms, then runs a short Monte Carlo-style projection (60s horizon, configurable) that weights commits by historical burstiness and active runways. Output is a small per-tenant summary: forecasted_headroom, commitment_conformance_ratio (CCR), and a confidence score. The gateway gate subscribes to aggregated prober signals and applies a graded policy: DRY_RUN -> SOFT_DROP (queue scoring / deprioritize) -> HARD_THROTTLE for tenants with CCR below threshold for >3 windows. All thresholds and weights are configurable on FleetPolicy and via console feature flags.

Checklist implemented: - [x] Commitment prober service and proto + in-memory cache - [x] Gateway gate integration with scoring hooks - [x] New telemetry (metrics + traces) and grafana dashboards - [x] FleetPolicy knobs and default safe values - [x] Canary rollout tooling (percent-of-tenants tag + rollout controller) - [x] Unit tests, integration tests, and perf harness workloads - [x] Documentation (console + API)

Commits (high level): - Add commitment prober service and limited projection engine - Expose prober signals via async pubsub to gateway - Implement backpressure gate and scoring logic in gateway request path - Add FleetPolicy schema fields and default profile - Add metrics: redwood.commitment_conformance_ratio, redwood.forecasted_headroom, redwood.gate_state - Add dashboards and runbook notes - Tests and canary rollout manifest

Files changed (high level): - services/prober/main.go - services/prober/projection.go - services/prober/README.md - gateway/backpressure/gate.go - gateway/backpressure/policy.go - api/fleetpolicy/v1beta1/types.go - telemetry/metrics/prometheus_rules.yml - observability/dashboards/commitment-conformance.json - tests/perf/commitment-prober-harness.yaml

Testing and results: Unit and integration tests were added for projection edge cases (zero activity, sustained burst, highly stochastic tenants). The perf harness ran synthetic mixed workloads (70% low-priority speculative, 30% committed) against a 32-GPU dedicated pool. Key results: - Baseline (no gate): 99th latency for committed requests: 430ms, CCR median: 0.78 - With gate (default safe profile): 99th latency for committed requests: 210ms, CCR median: 0.94 - Gate introduced ~1.8% increase in rejected speculative requests under peak; overall token throughput unchanged. We included an opt-out tag for tenants that must not be throttled.

Safety and rollout: Default behavior is DRY_RUN which surfaces signals to the console and telemetry only. Canary rollout will enable gating for a 10% tenant sample for 24h and then expand as metrics prove stable. Emergency kill-switch added to FleetPolicy and console. We included a reconciler to roll back gate state on configuration drift.

Backward compatibility: FleetPolicy additions are additive; gateways without the new subscription ignore prober signals. No breaking API changes.

Operational notes: New metrics to watch: redwood.commitment_conformance_ratio{tenant}, redwood.forecasted_headroom{region}, redwood.gate_state{tenant}. Alert rules recommended: CCR < 0.6 sustained for 5m -> P2, spike in forecasted_headroom delta -> P3. Runbook updated under observability/runbooks/commitment-conformance.md.

Related work: ENG-2042 (fleet stability initiative), ENG-2099 (autoscaler smoothing). This complements ongoing predictive headroom and warm-pool features.

Open items: - Monitor cross-tenant fairness signals; may add a global smoothing layer if oscillation detected - Expand probers to include spot preempt likelihood in future iteration

If you want to run locally: see services/prober/README.md for harness instructions and tests/perf/commitment-prober-harness.yaml for load profile.
